children: Xiaomi, Motorola and iQOO point to evolving consumer preferences for advanced processors, AI features and improved smartphone experiences despite higher component costs

India continues to be a key growth market for global smartphone manufacturers, with demand holding up despite rising memory and storage costs pushing up handset prices. Companies are seeing consumers place greater emphasis on advanced processors, artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities and overall user experience as smartphone purchasing preferences evolve.

At the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 in New Delhi, executives from Xiaomi, Motorola and iQOO highlighted these changing consumer preferences and outlined their upcoming flagship devices during interactions on the sidelines of a Qualcomm event at Yashobhoomi.

Gautam Batra, Associate Director – Product Marketing at Xiaomi, said consumers had adjusted to sustained increases in component costs and the resulting revisions in smartphone prices. Despite higher prices for random-access memory (RAM) and storage, the company continued to see healthy demand, suggesting that buyers had adapted to the changing pricing environment.

Batra described India as an important market for Xiaomi and other original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), citing its growth potential and consumers' aspirations for more advanced smartphones. He said the Indian market was growing faster than several other markets, reinforcing its importance to the company's business strategy.

On the product front, Batra said Xiaomi's newly unveiled Xiaomi 18 Pro flagship would feature Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 platform across international and Indian markets. The device is expected to offer improvements in graphics processing, photography and AI performance.

Motorola also highlighted changing consumer expectations, with buyers increasingly assessing smartphones on the quality of the experience they offer rather than technical specifications alone. Shivam Ranjan, Marketing Head – APAC at Motorola, said Indian consumers were becoming more discerning and placing greater emphasis on human-centric features and practical usability.

Ranjan previewed Motorola's upcoming Signature 27 handset, scheduled for release in 2026. The device is expected to be among the early smartphones powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon 6 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset. Its planned features include camera capabilities, agentic AI and a design intended to address evolving consumer requirements.

Meanwhile, iQOO announced its upcoming flagship, the iQOO 16, which will be powered by Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 platform. Nipun Marya, CEO of iQOO, said the smartphone would launch in India soon and represent the company's fastest device to date.
Marya added that further details of the company's collaboration with Qualcomm would be announced at a later stage.
